text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English clergyman CHARLES KINGSLEY, who wrote "The Water Babies" and "Westward Ho!", was born in 1819.
Former United States President GEORGE BUSH was born in 1924.
American singer VIC DAMONE (VITO FARINOLA), whose biggest hit was with "The Street Where Your Live" from the film "My Fair Lady", was born in 1928.
Dutch Jewish schoolgirl ANNE FRANK, who wrote her famous diary while in hiding from the Nazis, was born in 1929. She died in a German concentration camp on the 12th of March, 1945.
British underground folk-rock singer ROY HARPER, who sang with Pink Floyd on "Have A Cigar" (Led Zeppelin's "Hats Off To Mr Harper" was dedicated to him), was born in 1941.
British bass player PETE FARNDON, a founder member of 'The Pretenders' (who died on the 14th of April, 1983), was born in 1952.
Former Australian cricketer TERRY ALDERMAN was born in 1956.
** EVENTS **
1667 : LOUIS XIV's personal physician JEAN-BAPTISTE DENYS
successfully tranfused blood from a sheep to a 15 year old boy.
1809 : NAPOLEON BONAPARTE was excommunicated by POPE PIUS
VII.
1839 : A new kind of game known as "baseball" was played
in New York. Reported to be the invention of ABNER DOUBLEDAY, the new game bore similarities to the English 'rounders' and the childrens' game 'old cat'.
1931 : Severe flooding struck the Dubbo district of New
South Wales, isolating many towns in the region.
1931 : Notorious Chicago gang leader AL CAPONE and 73
henchmen were charged with 5,000 offences following investigations by the elite force known as the 'Untouchables'.
1935 : A truce ended the Chaco War, a conflict fought
between Bolivia and Paraguay during 1932-35.
1944 : Chinese Communist leader MAO ZEDONG announced that
he would support Nationalist leader CHIANG KAI-SHEK in the war against Japan.
1956 : The Australian state governments began a free mass
vaccination programme with Salk polio vaccine.
1957 : American band leader JIMMY DORSEY died.
1963 : Civil rights lawyer MEDGAR EVERS was murdered in
Mississippi by white racists.
1965 : The Beatles members were each awarded an MBE in
the Queen's birthday honours list.
1975 : A judge ruled Indian Prime Minister INDIRA
GANDHI's landslide election victory invalid, because civil servants had aided her campaign.
1978 : DAVID BERKOWITZ was given life sentences for each
of the six so-called 'Son of Sam' murders in New York.
1979 : American BRYAN ALLEN pedalled his way across the
English Channel in a man-powered aircraft, winning a 185,000 dollar prize.
1987 : QUEEN ELIZABETH II awarded her daughter, PRINCESS
ANNE, the title of Princess Royal.
1991 : Russians went to the polls in the country's
first-ever democratic elections. BORIS YELTSIN would emerge as the favourite of the people.
1991 : The people of Leningrad voted 55 per cent to 43
per cent to change the name of their city back to Saint Petersburg.
1991 : Mount Pinatubo, a Philippine volcano, erupted for
a third time just 14 hours after unleashing a series of explosions that shut down the biggest U.S. air base in Asia. The volcano had been dormant for six centuries.
1994 : Rebbe MENACHEM SCHNEERSON, the head of the
ultra-Orthodox Lubavitch movement and a figure of great religious power in Judaism, died in New York.
